As per allegations, the petitioner in collusion with one Parveen Saharan and Karambir Singh (since deceased) had cheated the complainant by issuing a forged allotment letter/possession letter of a plot after receiving Rs.3,21,048/ Rs.3,21,048/-.
Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.

He further contends that the complainant had filed complaint against Swadesh Boora @ Sudesh Boora, Samunder Boora, Jagbir Poonia and Krishna Bhagana and there were specific allegations of committing fraud against them but police in collusion with them have exonerated them and lodged FIR against the petitioner oner and one another person.
He further contends that no specific role has been attributed to the petitioner and he has no concern with the said incident.
It has also been contended that the petitioner has been roped in the present FIR only on the basis of incomplete affidavit submitted by co-accused accused Parveen Saharan.

Apart from the affidavit,
there is no other evidence to connect the petitioner with the offence in question.
He further submits that the petitioner has clean antecedents.
Learned counsel furthe furtherr submits that the petitioner is ready and willing to join the investigation as and when called upon to do so by the investigating agency.

On the other hand, learned State counsel while referring to the status report, has opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory nticipatory bail, by submitting that the allegations levelled against the petitioner are serious in nature.

He has further submitted that the petitioner, in connivance with co co-accused accused Parveen Saharan, had cheated the complainant by preparing a forged allotment allotment letter/possession letter and received an amount of Rs.3,21,048/-
However, he has admitted the fact that the petitioner is not involved in any other case.
Adjourned to 04.02.2026.
authenticity of this document.

- In the meantime, the petitioner is directed to join investigation within a week from today and would appear as and when required by the Investigating Officer and cooperate with the Investigating Agency.
In the event of arrest, he shall be admitted to interim bail on furnishing of bail/surety bonds to the satisfaction of Arresting/Investigating Officer.
The petitioner shall also abide by the conditions as envisaged under Section 482(2) of BNSS, 2023."

4. Learned counsel for the State, on instructions from ASI Raj Kumar,, has submitted that the petitioner has joined the investigation and is no longer required for further investigation.
5. In view off the statement made by learned State counsel, the interim order dated 15.01.2026 passed by this Court, is made absolute.
The petitioner shall continue to join investigation, as and when called by the Investigating Officer and shall also abide by the condi conditions tions as provided under Section 482(2) of the BNSS.
